WITNESS II
Sister ANNA ELISA SCRÒ

Procedural scope: Session III of 23 December 1995 (Proc. p. 275).

Name, surname, date and place of birth: Sister A. Maria Scrò, in religion Elisa, born in Marineo on 1 June 1913.

State and profession: Religious Daughter of Saint Anne, wardrobe keeper.

Quality of the witness: De auditu a videntibus (hearsay from eyewitnesses).

Observations on the witness and on the content of the testimony: The witness expresses admiration for the Servant of God's virtues, in particular her heroic poverty and heroic temperance. She also attests with conviction to the reputation for holiness the Servant of God enjoyed in life and to this day. She gives information about the reason the Process was interrupted.

§ 298
General information about the witness.

Ad 2 interr., proc. pag. 275, testis respondit:

My name is Sister A. Maria Scrò (in religion Elisa), daughter of the late Antonino and Guarnieri Antonina, born in Marineo on 1 June 1913, residing in Monreale in our religious House; I hold the office of wardrobe keeper.

§ 299
Esteem for the Servant of God.

Ad 3:1) I hold much esteem and veneration for the Servant of God, who was part of our religious Institute.

2) I was invited to give my testimony to contribute to the Servant of God's Beatification.

3) I received no suggestions regarding my testimony.

§ 300
Sources of her knowledge.

Ad 4: The first information about the Servant of God I had from my Novice Mistress. Afterwards, I enriched my knowledge of the life of Sister A. del Salvatore Orsi by reading an old biography of hers, whose author I do not know, and the more recent biography written by Sister A. Roberta Frati. And I can say - in my judgment - that the old biography is more complete than the latter.

Ad 7: 1-2) On the Servant of God's life and, particularly, on the virtues she practiced, I especially admired what follows.

§ 301
Heroic poverty.

The sense of truly heroic poverty that stands out from the fact that the Servant of God, in the religious Community, had no bed of her own and preferred to rest lying on the altar step.

§ 302
Prompt obedience.

The heroism of her obedience, shown, for example, when she complied with the Foundress's order sending her to our House in Trapani, and she obeyed, despite her grave illness and fever that forced her to stay in bed and which was perhaps the cause of her death.

§ 303
Spirit of penance and mortification.

Lastly, her spirit of penance and mortification was also - in my view - heroic, to the point of eating only the community's table scraps and, at times, the chicken feed.

§ 304
Heroic fortitude amid trial.

It also seems heroic to me how the Servant of God behaved at the most dramatic moments of her life. She was, indeed, strongly slandered by her fellow Sisters before the Foundress, who, as punishment, was about to take her veil from her. In that circumstance, the Servant of God, feeling strongly and wholly bound to God, answered the Foundress: "I received the veil before the altar, and if she wishes, I shall return it before the altar."

3) In my opinion, the Servant of God's principal activity took place in Sicily, when she was named Provincial Superior by the Foundress.

4) I consider that the distinguishing marks of the Servant of God's spirituality are to be found in the exercise of the virtues I have related above.

5) I repeat that I have devotion to the Servant of God.

§ 305
Esteemed in life, and after death called "the Little Saint of Palermo".

6-7) I also learned from my Novice Mistress that the Servant of God, in Palermo, was esteemed as a holy Sister while she was still alive, and, after her death, her reputation for holiness spread among the faithful, who called her "the Little Saint of Palermo".

§ 306
In the Institute's houses, she is regarded as a saint.

I entered the religious Institute of the Daughters of St. Anne in 1930 and, from then until today, in the various houses of ours where I have lived, Sister A. del Salvatore has always been esteemed and venerated as a saint.

8) I am not aware of any person or writing contrary to the Servant of God's reputation for holiness or to this Cause.

Instante Promotore: Is it known to you whether and when this cause of beatification had been begun, and why it was interrupted?

§ 307
Why the Cause of Beatification was interrupted.

Answer: I learned from the Novice Mistress that, almost immediately after the Servant of God's death, the Cause of Beatification was opened, but after some years it was interrupted in order to open the cause of Beatification of our Foundress.

§ 308
Place where she was buried.

Ad 8: 1) At first, the Servant of God was buried in a ground-level tomb in the Cemetery of "St. Ursula" in Palermo; afterwards (I cannot say precisely when) she was buried in our family chapel, in the same cemetery.

§ 309
The Foundress held her in great esteem.

I learned that the Mother Foundress came to Palermo some years after the Servant of God's death. On that occasion, the Foundress requested the canonical identification of the remains. This - in my opinion - shows that the Foundress too held her virtues in great esteem.

§ 310
The Servant of God's tomb is visited by many of the faithful.

2) During my stay in Palermo, I could observe that the Servant of God's tomb was frequently visited by the faithful, for devotional purposes, and people would sign their names on the tombstone.

I too went several times to visit the said tomb out of devotion, and I signed my name there as well.

3) As far as I am aware, no public cult has ever been paid to the Servant of God.

§ 311
No public cult has ever been paid.

Only the holy cards prepared by the Postulation and distributed by us, her fellow Sisters, are published.

4) I am not aware of any miracle obtained through the Servant of God's intercession.

WITNESS III
Sister ANNA TERESINA LO BUE

Procedural scope: Session IV of 27 December 1995 (Proc. p. 279).

Name, surname, date and place of birth: Lo Bue Carmela, in religion Sister Anna Teresina, born on 28 February 1920 in Calatafimi.

State and profession: Religious Daughter of Saint Anne, former teacher and superior.

Quality of the witness: De auditu a videntibus (hearsay from eyewitnesses).

Observations on the witness and on the content of the testimony: The witness affirms the continuity of the Servant of God's reputation for holiness, which she learned of from her entry into the Institute through the accounts of the older Sisters. She points to humility as the Servant of God's characteristic virtue, along with charity towards the poor and prayer.

Ad 2 interr., proc. pag. 279, testis respondit:

§ 312
General information about the witness.

My name is Lo Bue Carmela, in religion Sister A. Teresina, daughter of the late Carmelo and Giuseppina Consiglio, born in Casteltermini (AG) on 28 February 1920, residing in Palermo in our Provincial House.

I have been a professed religious in the Institute of the Daughters of St. Anne since 1943. For many years I was a teacher in our schools. I was also superior in one of our Houses in Caltanissetta.

Ad 3: 1) Since I am a Sister in the same Institute of which the Servant of God was a part, I am bound to her by this spiritual tie and by the esteem and veneration I hold for her.

2) I was invited by the Superior to give my testimony, and I present myself gladly, wishing to contribute to the Servant of God's Beatification.

3) I received no instructions or suggestions regarding my testimony.

§ 313
Sources of her knowledge.

Ad 4: I had the first information about the Servant of God during my postulancy and novitiate, both through what the mistress told us and through the recollections of the older Sisters.

§ 314
Humble endurance of trials.

Ad 7: 1) Of the Servant of God's life, I admired above all her humble endurance, shown when she was threatened by our Mother Foundress with expulsion from the Institute because of slander.

§ 315
Characteristic virtue: humility.

2) Therefore - in my opinion - the virtue that stands out most in her life is humility.

§ 316
Practiced all the virtues to a heroic degree.

From what I heard said in the Community by the older Sisters, who spoke of the Servant of God as a saint, I must consider that she practiced all the virtues to a heroic degree.

3) I learned that the Servant of God was sent by our Foundress as Provincial Superior of the Houses existing in Sicily.

§ 317
Was hosted in Palermo by Fr. Cusmano.

I also learned that, at the beginning, she was hosted by the Boccone Sisters, through the involvement of their Founder, Fr. Giacomo Cusmano, now Blessed. I also know that Cardinal Celesia, Archbishop of Palermo, appreciated the Servant of God's work.

§ 318
Charity towards the poor, penance, and prayer.

4) As to my own knowledge, besides the Servant of God's great humility, I can add that distinguishing marks of her spirituality were charity towards the poor and her spirit of penance and prayer, so much so that she preferred to sleep on the altar step.

5) I hold not only esteem but also devotion for the Servant of God, to whom I turn in my prayers.

§ 319
Reputation for holiness after death.

6) I learned that, almost immediately after her death, the Servant of God was regarded by everyone in Palermo as a saint, and the ecclesiastical authority opened the cause of beatification. I also learned that, after some time, this Cause was interrupted, but I do not know the reason; however, there is talk in the Community that the said interruption was due to the priority that was given to our Foundress's Cause.

§ 320
In the Communities, the Servant of God has always been spoken of with fervour and devotion.

7) I can affirm, in good conscience, that within our Sicilian Communities I have always heard the Servant of God spoken of as a model of holiness. Particularly in our House "Mater Gratiae" in Palermo, which for a long time was the Provincial seat of our Sicilian Communities. The Servant of God has always been spoken of with fervour and devotion, regarded as a true saint.

8) I am not aware of any person or writing contrary to the Servant of God's reputation for holiness or to this cause of beatification.

Ad 8: 1-2) The Servant of God was buried in a ground-level tomb, in the Cemetery of "St. Ursula" in Palermo.

I remember this tomb well because I went to visit it many times and always saw it full of flowers, which the faithful who came to visit certainly left there.

§ 321
Many devotees went to the tomb.

I learned, indeed, that many devotees went to that tomb to implore the Servant of God's intercession, in order to obtain graces from the Lord.

I do not recall precisely when the remains were moved from that tomb to the family chapel of our Institute, in the same cemetery.

§ 322
Transfer of the remains to the chapel.

I was present at the ceremony together with the other Sisters, and I recall that Msgr. Aglialoro, who was the Auxiliary Bishop of Palermo, also came.

I have not gone back to visit the Servant of God's tomb since, and I learned that, ever since it was decided to resume the cause of Beatification, her reputation for holiness has spread anew in Palermo.

§ 323
Graces have been obtained through the Servant of God's intercession.

3) I am not aware that, in Palermo or elsewhere, public cult has been granted to the Servant of God; only the holy cards printed by the Postulation circulate.

4) I heard it said that, through the Servant of God's intercession, graces have been obtained, but I do not know the particulars.

I recall at this moment that, some years back, a man came and told me, as I was at the porter's lodge, that his sister had received a grace as a result of prayers addressed to the Servant of God, but he gave me no further details.

WITNESS IV
Sister ANNA VINCENZA LO BUE

Procedural scope: Session V of 28 December 1995 (Proc. p. 283)

Name, surname, date and place of birth: Giuseppina Lo Bue, in religion Sister Anna Vincenza, born on 27 September 1915 in Casteltermini (AG).

State and profession: Religious Daughter of Saint Anne.

Quality of the witness: De auditu a videntibus (hearsay from eyewitnesses).

Observations on the witness and on the content of the testimony: The witness relates how the Servant of God's reputation for holiness remains very much alive and how her tomb is, now as in the past, a destination for devotees who gather there in prayer and leave flowers. The witness names prayer and penance as the Servant of God's characteristic virtues, and recalls her heroic humility and fortitude, which shone in her above all at the difficult moment of trial.

Ad 2 interr., proc. pag. 283, testis respondit:

§ 324
General information about the witness.

I am Lo Bue Giuseppina, in religion Sister A. Vincenza, daughter of the late Carmelo and Giuseppina Consiglio, born in Casteltermini (AG) on 27 September 1915, residing in Palermo in our Provincial House.

I have been a professed religious in the Institute of the Daughters of St. Anne since 1943 and have been responsible for the Community's necessary tasks.

Ad 3: 1) I am a member of the same Institute in which the Servant of God was a religious. I esteem her because I have always heard her spoken of as an exemplary religious.

2) I present myself gladly to contribute to the outcome of this Cause.

3) I received no instructions or suggestions.

§ 325
Sources of her knowledge of, and esteem for, the Servant of God.

Ad 4: Since my entry into my Community, I have always heard the older Sisters speak favourably of the Servant of God.

§ 326
Spirit of prayer and penance.

Ad 7: 1-2) Among the most significant facts of her life and among her virtues, I especially admired her spirit of prayer and penance. Indeed, I learned that she carried out her duties during the day, while spending the night hours in prayer before the Blessed Sacrament, and, when overcome by sleep, rested by lying down on the altar step itself.

§ 327
Humility.

I also learned that she humbly undertook all the work needed in the Community, without making use of her office as Provincial Superior.

It is known to me that the Servant of God practiced charity in the service of the sick and the poor, in keeping with the Foundress's chief idea, and almost in keeping with the spirit of charity of the Boccone Sisters, founded by Blessed Giacomo Cusmano, with whom, at first, she was housed in Palermo.

§ 328
Charity towards the sick.

3) She received from the Foundress the charge of Provincial Superior for Sicily, where some of our Houses already existed.

§ 329
Foremost virtues: piety, penance, humility, charity.

4) I repeat that - in my judgment - in the Servant of God her spirit of piety and penance, her humility and her charity are the most notable.

5) I hold esteem for the Servant of God, though I cannot call it devotion.

§ 330
Reputation for holiness.

6-7) I reaffirm that, since I entered our Institute, I have always heard the Servant of God spoken of, particularly by the older Sisters, as a holy religious.

8) I have never heard any voice contrary to the Servant of God's reputation for holiness.

Ad 8: 1-2) I recall having gone several times to visit the Servant of God's tomb, both when it was at ground level and when she was placed in the chapel of our Institute, situated in the Cemetery of "St. Ursula".

§ 331
Many visit her tomb to obtain graces through her intercession.

I learned that the faithful of Palermo frequently visited the Servant of God's first tomb and, for devotional purposes, would write their names on the marble slab and leave flowers there. I, because of my ailments, stay almost always inside the Institute, and I no longer go to visit the Servant of God's tomb, but I hear that the faithful still show their devotion by going to visit the new tomb.

3) I am not aware of any manifestation of public cult towards the Servant of God. I know that the holy cards prepared by the postulation circulate.

4) I do not know whether graces have been obtained through the Servant of God's intercession.

§ 332
Heroic humility at the moment of trial.

Ad 9: Having heard my testimony read back, I would like to add an episode from the Servant of God's life which I admired and which I recall at this moment. I learned that, following certain slanders suffered by the Servant of God in a Community in northern Italy, the Foundress was almost compelled to take her veil from her; in that situation, the Servant of God offered no resistance nor made excuses, but humbly said to the Mother: "you gave me the veil in church before the image of St. Anne, and I ask leave to request that it be taken from me before that same image".

The Foundress, who held the Servant of God in such high esteem, admired her humility and spared her the threatened punishment. I confirm my testimony under oath.

WITNESS V
Sister ANNA SILVINA MARGIOTTA

Procedural scope: Session VI of 30 December 1995 (Proc. p. 287).

Name, surname, date and place of birth: Dorotea Margiotta, in religion Sister Anna Silvina, born on 3 October 1923 in Mazzarino (CL).

State and profession: Religious Daughter of Saint Anne, nurse.

Quality of the witness: De auditu (by hearsay).

Observations on the witness and on the content of the testimony: The witness currently tends the Servant of God's tomb and relates how it is a place of devotion for many of the faithful, who leave flowers there, pause in prayer, and take her holy cards, further underscoring her reputation for holiness. She also relates that, even in life, the Servant of God was called "the little saint".

Ad 2 interr., proc. pag. 287, testis respondit:

§ 333
General information about the witness.

My name is Margiotta Dorotea, in religion Sister Anna Silvina, daughter of the late Francesco and Trapani Agnese. Born in Mazzarino (CL) on 3 October 1923, residing in Palermo in our Institute at Villa delle Rose. I attend to the care of the sick in our house.

Ad 3: 1) I hold esteem and devotion for the Servant of God.

2) I present myself gladly to testify in order to contribute to the purpose of this Cause.

3) I received no suggestions regarding my testimony.

§ 334
Sources of her knowledge.

Ad 4: I had the first information about the Servant of God when I entered the Institute; now she is spoken of more often, and I have broadened my knowledge of her life by reading a short biography of her.

§ 335
Humility and charity.

Ad 7: 1-2-3-4) In the Servant of God, I particularly admired her humility and her charity, virtues she also exercised in Sicily when she was named Provincial Superior.

I read, indeed, that the Servant of God was slandered, and she knew how to patiently bear these humiliations. With great humility and charity, she devoted herself to attending the sick at home.

5) I repeat that I have devotion to the Servant of God and that I often invoke her in my prayers.

§ 336
Her reputation for holiness is widespread among the communities and the faithful.

6-7) As to her reputation for holiness, I can only say that it has been spreading not only in our Communities but also among the faithful, particularly since it was decided to resume her Cause of beatification. However, I heard it said that the Servant of God, while she was still alive, was called by the people of Palermo "the little saint".

8) I have not heard any voice contrary to the Servant of God's reputation for holiness or to this cause of beatification.

§ 337
Exhumation of the remains and burial in the family chapel.

Ad 8: 1) The Servant of God was buried in the Cemetery of "St. Ursula" in Palermo, in an underground tomb. In 1957, if I recall correctly, she was transferred to the family chapel situated in the same cemetery. On that occasion, the canonical identification of her remains was carried out. I recall that the two doctors in charge of that identification were Dr. Iacono and Dr. Speciale, who worked at the "Ingrassia" sanatorium, where I was then a nurse.

§ 338
Her tomb draws the faithful, who go there to pray and leave flowers.

2) I went several times to visit the Servant of God's first tomb, and now every week I go to the new tomb, both to clean the chapel and out of personal devotion. I can attest that the Servant of God's two tombs were and are places that draw many of the faithful, who showed and still show their devotion by leaving flowers and pausing in prayer. Each week I am nearly obliged to bring holy cards of the Servant of God, prepared by the Postulation, to meet the faithful's constant requests.

3) I am not aware of any manifestation of improper public cult.

4) I learned that, through the Servant of God's intercession, various graces have been received.

§ 339
Graces obtained through the Servant of God's intercession.

About three months ago, a man told me that his daughter, confined to a wheelchair, was almost miraculously healed following prayers addressed to the Servant of God. He also told me that, since then, he always carries the Servant of God's holy card with him.

I have also known people who, through her intercession, obtained employment or reconciliation among family members.

WITNESS VI
Sister ANNA CARMELA LO BAIDO

Procedural scope: Session VII of 30 December 1995 (Proc. p. 291).

Name, surname, date and place of birth: Caterina Lo Baido, in religion Sister Anna Carmela, born on 26 September 1921 in Partinico.

State and profession: Religious Daughter of Saint Anne, secretary of the school located in the Provincial House.

Quality of the witness: De auditu (by hearsay).

Observations on the witness and on the content of the testimony: The witness learned about the Servant of God from her entry into the Institute of the Daughters of St. Anne; she regularly visited the Servant of God's former burial place, observing the signs of the great numbers of devotees who went there to pray.

§ 340
General information about the witness.

Ad 2 interr., proc., pag. 291, testis respondit:

My name is Caterina Lo Baido, in religion Sister Anna Carmela, daughter of the late Gaspare and Galati Maria, born in Partinico on 26 September 1921, residing in Palermo in our Provincial House. I obtained a teaching diploma and currently assist the secretary of our school.

Ad 3: 1) I have been a professed religious since 1943 in the same religious Institute in which the Servant of God was a religious, for whom I hold esteem and devotion.

2) I was prompted by the Postulator to give my testimony, which I do gladly out of the devotion I hold for the Servant of God.

3) I received no suggestions regarding my testimony.

§ 341
Sources of her knowledge.

Ad 4: I received the first information about the Servant of God after my entry into the Institute, both from what the Mistress of postulants told us and from what circulated in the Community. I later broadened my knowledge by reading the book "Biographical Notes".

§ 342
Generous charity towards the poor and the sick.

Ad 7: 1-4) From what I learned and what I recall, I can say that the Servant of God, especially in Sicily, where she was sent as Provincial Superior, faithfully fulfilled what our Foundress desired, devoting herself with great and generous charity to the service of the sick at home and of the poor.

I also learned that the Servant of God loved poverty.

5) My devotion to the Servant of God is sincere, and I always turn to her in my prayers.

§ 343
Reputation for holiness.

6-7) I can say that, from the time I first learned of the Servant of God, she was spoken of, and often, as a saint.

8) No rumours contradicting the Servant of God's reputation for holiness ever reached me.

Ad 8: 1-2) The Servant of God was buried, as I myself could verify, in our tomb, below ground, in the Cemetery of "St. Ursula".

§ 344
Visitors signed their names on the tombstone.

I recall that visiting this tomb was always my favourite thing to do, and I did it with enthusiasm, because I felt something within me that bound me to her. Indeed, alongside the many signatures I found written on the tomb's marble slab, I too wanted to add my own, as if to tell the Servant of God to remember me.

I must consider that all those numerous signatures I observed showed the influx of the faithful who went to pray at that tomb.

§ 345
Canonical identification of the Servant of God's remains.

I learned that, many years ago, the Servant of God's remains were exhumed and the canonical identification carried out; they were reassembled inside a small casket placed in the family chapel of our Institute, in the same cemetery.

I also learned that at this new tomb too there is an influx of the faithful who come to invoke her protection.

§ 346
Absence of public cult.

3) I can attest that improper public cult has never been paid to the Servant of God. Only the holy cards with the proper ecclesiastical authorisation circulate.

4) I heard it said that, through the Servant of God's intercession, some grace has been received. But I cannot give the particulars.

WITNESS VII
Sister ANNA GAETANINA ZUPONE

Procedural scope: Session IX of 19 May 1998 (Proc. p. 311).

Name, surname, date and place of birth: Maria Giuseppa Zupone, in religion Sister Anna Gaetanina, born on 1 May 1932 in Conversano (BA).

State and profession: Religious Daughter of Saint Anne, superior.

Quality of the witness: De auditu (by hearsay).

Observations on the witness and on the content of the testimony: The witness highlights the reputation for holiness that the Servant of God enjoyed and still enjoys within the Institute and among the people of Palermo. She also expresses the conviction that the Servant of God can be a model of Christian life for people today; she further recalls the prophecies that Sister Anna del Salvatore made to the Foundress Rosa Gattorno.

Ad 2 interr., proc. pag. 311, testis respondit:

§ 347
General information about the witness.

My name is Maria Giuseppa Zupone, in religion Sister A. Gaetanina, daughter of the late Vitantonio and Coletta Angela, born in Conversano (BA) on 1 May 1932. I live in Rome, at Via Merulana 177. I have been a professed religious among the Daughters of St. Anne since 1954. I served in the general secretariat, first as an assistant and then as secretary general. I worked as a teacher, as local superior in Messina, Ferrara, and Palermo, and as Provincial Superior in Sicily. I am currently superior of the Generalate House in Rome. I obtained a teaching qualification and a degree in Sacred Sciences at the Urbaniana.

Ad 3: I belong to the same religious Institute as the Servant of God Sister Anna del Salvatore Orsi, and I am moved to testify for having heard her spoken of repeatedly, and by a great many fellow Sisters. I give my testimony freely and spontaneously, at the Postulator's invitation.

§ 348
Sources of her knowledge.

Ad 4: I state that I learned what concerns the Servant of God de auditu (by hearsay) and that I read a biography of her, Historical Notes on the Life of Sister Anna del Salvatore Orsi, Professed Religious of the Order of the Daughters of St. Anne, Rome 1893, and also the booklet by Roberta Cecilia Frati, Sister Anna del Salvatore Orsi, Elle Di Ci, Turin 1995.

§ 349
Writings of the Servant of God.
§ 350
Prophecies concerning the Foundress.
§ 351
The Servant of God, a model of Christian commitment.

Ad 5: I am aware that, in the archive of the Generalate House, there is correspondence concerning the Servant of God. I know some excerpts of Sister A. del Salvatore Orsi's letters; very confidential letters that express her relationship with the Foundress. Mother Rosa Gattorno herself held Sr. A. Orsi in great esteem and entrusted herself to her prayers. On the other hand, it seems that Sister A. del Salvatore foretold that, upon the Foundress's death, her body would remain incorrupt, that she would be buried among her daughters, and that one day we would see her in St. Peter's, among the glory of the Founders.

Ad 7: 1) In my view, the Servant of God can, in the present historical moment, give a great impetus and be a model for us, Daughters of St. Anne, and for all those in the Church committed to going out to the poor and, in particular, to those who suffer.

§ 352
Humility and spirit of sacrifice.

2) The Servant of God was marked by great humility and a spirit of sacrifice, both in the community where she lived and towards the poorest; wherever she passed, she always brought a touch of peace and serenity. She was always distinguished by her maternal spirit, by obedience, poverty, and simplicity, virtues all lived in a heroic way.

§ 353
Virtues lived heroically.
§ 354
Characteristic virtues: poverty of heart and maternal self-giving.

3) The Servant of God came to Sicily to open a community of nursing Sisters. She was immediately esteemed and appreciated by all: religious and civil authorities, Sisters, and the people. A few years after her arrival in Palermo, the Foundress gave her the task of coordinating the various communities of Sicily as Provincial Superior.

4) In my judgment, the distinguishing marks of the Servant of God's spirituality are poverty of heart and maternal self-giving.

5) I believe that the Servant of God can point today's world towards the Father's merciful love.

6) I have devotion to the Servant of God; I feel her as a sister, and I entrust myself to her to accompany me in daily life.

§ 355
The cause was resumed by the will of the 1984 General Chapter.

7) In our Congregation, the Servant of God has always been held in great esteem. It was a proposal of the 1984 General Chapter that promoted the resumption of the Servant of God's Cause, lamenting its interruption. Moreover, when the ecclesial community in Albareto celebrated the 150th anniversary of Sister A. del Salvatore's birth, we felt even more encouraged to resume the process.

§ 356
Reputation for holiness in Palermo and in her native town.

There is a tradition in Palermo and in the Institute concerning her reputation for holiness; her tomb is a continual point of reference for many people, who express their devotion through simple and meaningful gestures (flowers, candles, requesting and using her holy cards).

§ 357
Letter "for a grace received".

8) I am not aware of anyone contradicting the Servant of God's reputation for holiness; on the contrary, I know that many people believe they have received favours from the Servant of God. I could cite many episodes; in particular, I recall that a gentleman sent me a letter in which he states that he received a grace on behalf of his sick daughter.

Archiepiscopal Delegate: Can Sister Gaetanina Zupone show the tribunal this letter referred to as "for a grace received"?

Answer: this letter is kept in the provincial archive of Palermo.

§ 358
Burial and exhumation.

Ad 8: 1) The Servant of God's remains were buried in the Cemetery of St. Ursula, where they currently rest. She was first interred in bare earth; she was later exhumed and placed in the new small chapel owned by the Institute.

§ 359
Many people pray before her tomb.

2-4) At the request of the Sisters and the people, a picture was prepared and placed just behind the gate of the chapel itself, which draws many people. I myself have seen various people praying before the Servant of God's tomb, as I also do when I have the chance.

I have no knowledge of the existence of relics of the Servant of God, nor am I aware that public cult is paid to her.

WITNESS VIII
Sister ANNA IRENE CADONI

Procedural scope: Session X of 19 May 1998 (Proc. p. 318).

Name, surname, date and place of birth: Sister Anna Irene Cadoni, in the world Andreana, born on 27 April 1921 in Oristano.

State and profession: Religious Daughter of Saint Anne, in charge of the Institute's general secretariat.

Quality of the witness: De auditu (by hearsay).

Observations on the witness and on the content of the testimony: The witness considers the Foundress Rosa Gattorno's opinion of, and esteem for, the Servant of God to be highly significant, and expresses the conviction that the Servant of God practiced the virtues to a heroic degree, in particular faith, love of God, and poverty. The witness prayed to the Servant of God during her own illnesses and those of her family, and received help.

Ad 2 interr., proc. pag. 318, testis respondit:

§ 360
General information about the witness.

Sources of his knowledge.

Her faith, humility, prayer, and dedication are admired.

The witness has spread knowledge of the Servant of God.

Sources of her knowledge.

Her reputation for holiness persists among her fellow Sisters.

Annual commemoration, in Albareto, of her birth.

Prophecy of the Servant of God.

Model of simplicity and dedication.

A very much alive reputation for holiness in the Institute.

Prophecies of the Servant of God concerning the Foundress.

Writings of the Servant of God.

Ordinary life lived heroically.

§ 434
Heroic spirit of sacrifice.
§ 435
Example of total abandonment to God.
§ 436
Invocation of the Servant of God during the Second World War.

My devotion to the Servant of God arises, above all, from the fact that she is my fellow townswoman, and I also feel I share a certain affinity of temperament with her.

§ 437
Reputation for holiness always alive.

Grace obtained through the Servant of God's intercession.

The Servant of God's tomb, a destination for visitors.

Humility, dedication to those in need, fortitude amid adversity.

I recall that some time ago I asked some Sisters for news about their Foundress's process, and I noticed, to my great surprise, that they all showed much more enthusiasm and interest in Sister Anna del Salvatore's process, thereby showing a particular esteem for the Servant of God, whom, they said, they felt much closer to, and they were very pleased about the ongoing process.

8) I am not aware of any people, or any writings, opposed to the Servant of God's reputation for holiness, nor of anyone having opposed her cause.

Ad 8: 1-3) The Servant of God was buried, and still today rests, in the cemetery of St. Ursula in Palermo. I have stopped before her tomb several times to admire it and so that she would pray for me.

4) I am not aware of any miracles or graces having occurred through the Servant of God's intercession.

Below are brief biographical notes on some of the figures most frequently encountered in the Summarium.

Accinelli Antonio, priest. He was born in Genoa in 1825. Ordained a priest, he carried out his ministry largely at the metropolitan church of "San Lorenzo", of which he was custodian from 1873. A friend of the Gattorno household, he was very close to Mother Rosa, whom he esteemed as a person worthy of honour and respect for her uncommon qualities and for the distinguished mission to which the Lord had called her. For this reason he was a faithful and enthusiastic collaborator in the houses she founded in Liguria and Piedmont. While still very young, he came to know the Servant of God Sister Anna del Salvatore, who was assigned to the Community of Genoa-Sampierdarena and to Sestri, and he came to appreciate her goodness and capacity for sacrifice, also evident in her letters to Mother Gattorno.

Andreotti (Father Ottavio) Raffaele. Born in Piteglio (Pistoia) on 10 January 1837, he entered the Congregation of the Piarists on 28 March 1855 and, after devoting himself to teaching for some years, continued his clerical studies.

Ordained a priest in Castelfiorentino, he was assigned to Florence, where he taught at the San Carlo school. Having come to know Mother Rosa Gattorno and the Daughters of St. Anne, he did a great deal, especially in the early years, to help their establishment take root in the reality of the city and the Diocese; he formed a close friendship with the Foundress, to the point of asking her to be "associated" with the Institute of the Daughters of St. Anne (as is shown by an Archive document - AFSA, Florence Foundation). He devoted himself to teaching for over forty-five years and died on 25 July 1903, after a painful illness.

Bennicelli (Father) Antonio. Born in Rome on 18 December 1817 and died there in 1895. He entered the Order of Clerics Regular, Ministers of the Sick (Camillians), and made his profession on 26 June 1834. Ordained a priest on 26 April 1840 in Viterbo, he was appointed parish priest of the church of St. Mary Magdalene (attached to the general curia) and president of the Congregation of the Noble Ladies of Mary Assumed into Heaven. In 1865 he founded the "House of the Repentant Women" on Via dei Riarii, in the Lungara district, a work he wished to donate, in 1878, to the Daughters of St. Anne. The negotiations, which began well, were not concluded, however, because of the particular conditions placed on the Foundress Mother Rosa Gattorno. The Servant of God Sister Anna del Salvatore was assigned for a few months (November-December 1878) to this House.

Bertuzzi (Sister Anna Battistina) Rosalia. Born in Settima (PC) on 27 March 1849, she entered the Institute of the Daughters of St. Anne on 9 February 1872 and made her first Vows on 26 July 1875. From 1875 to 1879 she was in Mercatello (PS); then in Giuliano (NA) and, from 1883, in Palermo, as Superior of the Sisters serving at the "S. Francesco Saverio" Hospital. In 1885, after the Servant of God's death, she was appointed Provincial Superior of Sicily, an office she carried out with great zeal and maternal care until her death, which occurred in Palermo, at the "S. Nicolò all'Albergherìa" House, on 17 February 1913.

Bova Gaspare, priest. Born in Palermo on 2 January 1847, he was elected to the titular See of Samaria on 30 September 1896, as auxiliary to the Cardinal Archbishop of Palermo.

Calì Antonino, canon. Rector of the "Ardizzone" Orphanage in Palermo, he chose to entrust the Work's direction to the Daughters of St. Anne, who took it on in 1881. He knew Sister Anna del Salvatore very well and held her in great esteem.

Carrega (Sister Anna Benedetta) Anna. Daughter of Marquis Antonino Benedetto and Camilla D'Aste, she was born in Genoa on 28 May 1842. At the age of 11, having lost her mother, she went to Nice, to the religious French Ladies, where she received a formation suited to her social standing. In Genoa she came to know Mother Rosa Gattorno and was so deeply struck by her personality and by the good she accomplished in the social and ecclesial sphere that, in January 1874, she decided to follow her. She received the religious habit of the Daughters of St. Anne in the monastery of the Oblate Sisters of St. Frances of Rome, at Tor de' Specchi in Rome, where the Foundress had opened a school for poor girls. In 1875 she became Mother Gattorno's Secretary, and, upon the latter's death in 1900, was elected to succeed her as Superior General. She therefore knew Sister Anna del Salvatore very well and appreciated her virtues.

Cecconi Eugenio, archbishop. Born in Florence on 4 February 1834, he attended the Capranica College in Rome, earning a doctorate in theology. Consecrated bishop on 3 January 1875, he governed the Diocese of Florence from 1875 to 1888; he died on 15 June 1888. Having come to know the Foundress Mother Rosa Gattorno, he asked to have in Florence a Community of the Daughters of St. Anne devoted to home nursing care. He welcomed them paternally in November 1875. The Servant of God Sister Anna del Salvatore was the Community's first Superior.

Celesia Michelangelo, cardinal. He was born in Palermo on 13 January 1814 and died there on 15 April 1904. A Benedictine, he was for eight years Abbot General of the Cassinese Congregation; in 1860 he was appointed Bishop of Patti and, in 1871, transferred to the archbishopric of Palermo, where he was made a cardinal in 1884. He welcomed the Daughters of St. Anne into his diocese: in Termini Imerese in 1878 and in Palermo in 1880. From then on he came to know the Servant of God Sister Anna del Salvatore deeply, encouraging and supporting her in the founding of several Houses. He held her in the greatest esteem, entrusting her even with delicate tasks, and relied on her for missions of grave importance.

Ciaranfi Luigi, canon of the Metropolitan Church of Florence. He was delegate for monasteries. He died in Florence on 28 July 1908.

Cusmano Giacomo, blessed. Born on 15 March 1834 in Palermo, he attended the Jesuit school and, at 21, already a brilliant doctor, placed his profession entirely at the service of the poor. At 26 he received Priestly Ordination and soon founded the Association of the "Poor Man's Morsel." In 1880 he gave hospitality to the first community of the Daughters of St. Anne in Palermo, led by the Servant of God Sister Anna del Salvatore Orsi. That same year, he approached the Foundress Mother Rosa Gattorno to secure the Daughters of St. Anne for his work. However, the negotiation did not succeed, and he himself founded a new Congregation, the "Handmaids of the Poor," and, seven years later, the "Missionary Servants of the Poor." He died in Palermo on 14 March 1888.

Filiti Enrico, beneficiary canon. Canon of the Cathedral of Palermo, synodal Judge (archiepiscopal commission), pro-president of the commission for poor clerics, and supernumerary private chamberlain to His Holiness (22 September 1903). He was confessor to Sister Anna del Salvatore. He died in Palermo on 8 April 1919.

Franchi Alessandro, cardinal. He was born in Rome on 25 June 1819. Having graduated in theology at the Roman Seminary, he was then called to the Secretariat of State as a minute-writer. After holding important posts in Spain and, later, in Florence, in 1860 he took up, in Rome, the post of Secretary of the Congregation for Extraordinary Ecclesiastical Affairs. In 1868 he was sent as apostolic nuncio to Spain and, in 1871, as ambassador to Constantinople, to the Sultan. Made a cardinal in 1873, the following year he was appointed prefect of the Congregation of Propaganda Fide; and finally Secretary of State in 1878. In May of that same year he was assigned as Cardinal protector of the Daughters of St. Anne, an office he held for only a few months owing to his subsequent death.

Giovannini Attilio, monsignor. Born in 1840 in Borgo Santi Apostoli (FI), he died in Florence on 5 January 1928. He earned his doctorate in utroque iure at the Sapienza of Rome in 1862; he was ordained a priest in 1864. The following year he became professor of Sacred Scripture at the Florentine Seminary and, in 1874, was appointed parish priest of S. Lorenzo in Florence, the parish to which belonged the community of the Daughters of St. Anne, whom he supported, esteemed, and helped.

Laberiska Emilia, Princess of Fitalia. She was born on 21 June 1847 in Ohexie, in the governorate of Warsaw (Poland), and married, in Palermo in 1871, Prince Gerolamo Settimo of Fitalia. A great benefactress of the Daughters of St. Anne, she formed an affectionate friendship first with Sister Anna del Salvatore and, after her death, with the Foundress Mother Rosa Gattorno. Firmly set on the path of holiness, she was enrolled by Mother Rosa Gattorno in the Third Order of St. Anne. In Palermo and elsewhere she distinguished herself by her great love for the poor, by the consistent witness of her life, by the fervour of her piety, and by her leadership of the Pious Work of the Tabernacles - the Association of Perpetual Adoration and for Poor Churches - of which she was "president." She died in Palermo on 22 December 1927 and, in keeping with her wishes, was clothed in the humble habit of a Daughter of St. Anne.

Lancia di Brolo Domenico Gaspare, Archbishop of Monreale. A Benedictine of the Cassinese Congregation, he was born in Palermo on 1 October 1825, was consecrated bishop on 28 March 1878, and was promoted to the Archiepiscopal See of Monreale on 24 March 1884. An archbishop assistant to the Pontifical throne and Consultor of the Sacred Congregation of "Propaganda Fide", he was among those who signed the petition for the introduction of the Cause of Beatification of the Servant of God Anna del Salvatore. At Monreale he had occasion to know and appreciate Sister Anna del Salvatore's particular gifts and virtues.

Pennino Antonino, canon, Penitentiary of the Cathedral of Palermo. Ordained a priest on 19 September 1866, he was in Palermo confessor to Blessed Cusmano and, for more than thirty years, a prudent spiritual director to many souls eager to undertake a path of perfection.

Ricci Mauro, writer. He was born in Florence on 14 June 1826; he entered the Piarists on 17 September 1843. He died in Rome on 27 January 1900. He was in contact with the leading literary figures of his time; Leo XIII had him appointed professor of Italian literature at the higher school he had established in Rome.

He was Superior General of the Pious Schools from 1866 until his death. Among his extensive works are remembered: Vita della s. madre Teresa di Gesù, Florence 1874; Vita di cari defunti, ibid. 1875; L'Iliade travestita alla fiorentina, vols. 23, Florence 1884-1897; Dante Alighieri cattolico apostolico romano, ibid. 1885; I riposi Compiobbi, ibid. 1894; Prose sacre, morali e filosofiche, ibid. 1895; L'allegra filologia, ibid. 1898. (Enciclopedia Cattolica, Ente per l'Enciclopedia Cattolica e per il Libro Cattolico, Vatican City, vol. X, p. 872).

He oversaw the printing of the Prayer Book for the Daughters of St. Anne, Mother of the Immaculate Virgin, Florence, Tipografia Calasanziana, 1878.

Speranza (Sister Anna Celsa) Carolina, born in Sassuolo (Modena) on 30 June 1853.

After obtaining her elementary teaching diploma and teaching for four years in her hometown, she entered the Daughters of St. Anne in Piacenza, where she received the religious habit on 4 November 1876. Soon afterwards she was sent by the Foundress to Rome, as teacher and director in the Community of the "Parrocchietta" - desired by Pope Pius IX, now Blessed - and then in that of the Fornaci district, where she was also superior. From 1882 she was in charge of the general secretariat; shortly thereafter she was elected general assistant and remained at the Foundress's side until the latter's death. She was then elected Secretary General and, in 1915, upon the death of Sister A. Benedetta Carrega, succeeded her as Mother General until 1921, the year of her own death.

Valuable, for the precision of their details and the richness of their references, are the memoirs she wrote concerning the events experienced by the Foundress and the Institute in those years.

Zini Raffaello, Father Celestino. Born in Florence on 16 December 1825; he entered the Piarists on 15 December 1840. He was professor of history and philosophy, and rector of young Piarists; in 1864 he was appointed Rector of the Professed House of S. Giovannino in Florence; in 1872, by order of the Municipality, he became Director of Schools; in 1874 he was elected Moderator of the Piarist Province of Tuscany, an office in which he was confirmed for four three-year terms. In 1889 he was elected Bishop of Siena and, as a true shepherd, gave himself to his flock. He died in Siena on 19 May 1892, as a result of the exertions of his last pastoral visit. (from Alfonso Palchetti, Mons. Celestino Zini, in Zini Celestino, Scritti vari e Lettere, part I, Tipografia Calasanziana, Florence 1893).

Zuccaro Ignazio, monsignor, Bishop of Caltanissetta. Born in Palermo on 23 August 1839, he first attended the schools of the Oratorian Fathers, then went on to the Seminary. Ordained a priest, he worked for the restoration of the Oratorian community and was close to the charitable initiatives of Blessed Father Giacomo Cusmano. In Palermo he enjoyed a reputation as a good priest sensitive to the people's needs. Cardinal Celesia, Archbishop of Palermo, chose him as his secretary, appointed him Canon Treasurer of the Cathedral and, finally, his Vicar General. In 1896 he was appointed Bishop of Caltanissetta. He came to know the Daughters of St. Anne - called by the Archbishop to direct the College of Termini Imerese - in 1878, and, commissioned by that same Archbishop, welcomed with great kindness the Servant of God Sister Anna del Salvatore and the other Sisters who arrived with her in Palermo, helping them in every way to settle into the "house for the nurses" and later also in founding other houses in the Diocese of Palermo. He followed the Communities and the Sisters step by step, providing them with what they needed, and was a precious father, collaborator, and counselor to the Servant of God in every situation and need. Her sudden and untimely death grieved him greatly, and he did not fail, on various occasions, to sing her praises. He died on 28 November 1913.

Institute of the Daughters of St. Anne, Nurses

Via Cintorinai 48 - Palazzo Briuccia

Those who lie here enclosed in venerable deposit in this crypt are the mortal remains of Sister Anna del Salvatore Orsi, born in Albareto di Borgotaro, in the Parma countryside, to Angelo and Domenica Mussi, on 23 [22] February 1842.

From her earliest childhood she showed the most evident signs of divine favour, while, inclined to piety, recollection, and devotion, she kept herself entirely aloof from every childish frivolity... Instead she showed herself precocious in discernment, in prayer, and in virtue.

A candid flower blossoming fragrantly amid thorns and brambles, the young Maria Anna spent her adolescence wrapped at once in loveliness and purity, without the corrupting air of the age ever being able to cast the slightest shadow over her. So that, having reached the age at which youth lets itself be seduced by the illusions and vanities of the earth, our Maria Anna Orsi instead binds herself with the sweetest chains to Christ Jesus, donning in 1869 the religious habit of the recently founded Institute of the Daughters of St. Anne, whose spirit is nothing other than to serve God by serving one's neighbour.

No obstacles managed to turn her away... no protests from loving relatives availed... for Maria Anna del Salvatore is already in the Novitiate House in Piacenza, an example to her fellow Sisters, an edification to those in charge.

There the Lord shaped her with a singular spirit, there He made her understand the divine charisms; there He spoke to her in solitude, leading her along the path of perfect abandonment in the Sacred Heart of God!

And since charity towards God cannot remain idle, but, like a living flame, must show itself and burst forth, so Sister Anna del Salvatore, journeying from one Italian city to another, left her blessed footprints everywhere, assisting and consoling human infirmities wherever she went, and leaving behind her immense longing and infinite blessing.

And if the cities of Genoa, Milan, Florence, Macerata, Naples, and Rome had the fortune to possess, for a time, so great a treasure of virtue, our Palermo had the good fortune to see her within its walls in May 1880, assigned as Superior for this city, and in 1884 for the new Province of Sicily, where the Institute was only just being born. And it was a miracle of Providence how Sister Anna del Salvatore managed, in so short a time, to win the esteem and cooperation of everyone, ecclesiastical and civil Authorities, citizens of every rank and class, ladies, patricians, Priests, gentlemen, down to the humblest of the common people... so that, with everyone drawn by her beneficial attraction, the Institute of the Daughters of St. Anne rapidly spread its roots not only in this Capital but in almost all the main centres of the Island... an expansion that did not halt at her untimely and sorrowful departure, but which afterwards spread a thousandfold more, as though she had left behind a wide-sown seed of holy and marvelous growth.

And the Lord could not fail to delight in and favour the works of His Servant! Mortification, austerity, penance, prayer, prolonged fasts, continual sacrifices, boundless charity... and then endless modesty, recollection, perfect self-denial... These won for her every praise from men, every blessing from God!...

So that, finding her already prematurely fit for the crown, on 7 June 1885, after a brief illness in which Sister Anna del Salvatore shone in a thousand ways through obedience and resignation, He drew her untimely, amid the grief and prayers of all, to eternal rest!

And her memory has remained in honour among us! Taken from us, yes, and blessed by all, there forms in everyone the wish that, just as God will surely have glorified her in heaven, so He will also hasten her glorification by the Church here on earth! So be it!

The documentation presented here - mostly included in the Process and to a lesser extent extra-procedural - concerns the difficult period the Servant of God went through as Superior of the Community of the Daughters of St. Anne, in Florence.

The Institute, which in April 1876 had already received the Decretum laudis, could depend on the diocesan Ordinary only for the simple activity of apostolate, since its internal governance and administration were reserved to the Holy See.

The Community's Confessor and the Vicar for nuns did not understand this distinction, so that the misunderstandings that resulted affected not only the Servant of God personally, but also involved, besides the Community, the Institute itself.

The Bishop, not correctly informed, had at first decided to close the House, because of the presumed insubordination towards his lawful authority on the part of the Superior Sister Anna del Salvatore; but a few months later - having better understood the situation - he re-established good relations with the Institute, so that the Community could resume its mission calmly and fruitfully.

The documents subsequent to the Servant of God's departure from Florence (23 April 1878) fully reveal the extent of the matter, although, for the sake of brevity, only some of them are reproduced in the Summarium. They are nonetheless available, should anyone wish to consult them, in the Institute's Historical Archive (AFSA C.3.165).
